speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific feeding difficulties and bowel movements this 8-month-old boy is experiencing? Please also mention if he had any recent illnesses or surgeries.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the abdominal distension generalized or localized to a specific area, and has he passed any stool or gas recently? I will also examine his abdomen for any palpable masses or signs of peritonitis.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool recently, and if so, was it tarry or meconium-like? I would like to assess for signs of intestinal obstruction or Hirschsprung disease. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the infant ever passed meconium within the first 48 hours of life, and have you noticed any explosive watery stools or foul-smelling fecal incontinence? I would like to examine for a palpable "sausage-shaped" mass in the right upper quadrant. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the ultrasound is normal, I am less concerned about intussusception and more focused on Hirschsprung disease. When did he first pass his meconium after birth, and has he ever required a rectal exam or enema for relief? REQUEST TEST: Rectal Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unexpected result, as a normal biopsy effectively rules out Hirschsprung disease. Given the abdominal distension, feeding difficulties, and lack of fever or vomiting, could you describe the texture and frequency of his current stools, and has he had any episodes of bilious vomiting? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal CT Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and biopsy results, I am considering functional causes like severe constipation or an anatomical issue not visible on standard scans. Has he ever had a rectal suction biopsy during the newborn period, and does his abdomen feel hard or soft to the touch? REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease

speaker: Doctor
text: The contrast enema reveals a transition zone, which is the hallmark radiological sign of Hirschsprung disease despite the previous normal biopsy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
